Codex review: blocked before merge. ## What this changes This PR retains npm plugin artifacts, installation records, and settings so failed core updates can restore compatible plugins. **Example:** Core rolls back from 2026.9.36 to 2026.9.34 after upgrading plugins. - **Before:** Plugins requiring API 2026.9.36 remain installed and are skipped by core 2026.9.34. - **After:** Rollback restores the previous plugin artifacts, records, and matching settings before restarting core. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | The repair is valuable, but verified compatibility and wrapper defects block merge, and the persisted-format upgrade claims lack inspectable result artifacts. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 2 actionable review findings remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Partial **User problem:** After a failed update restores older core, installed plugins can remain too new to load. **Reason:** Compatible plugin restoration has clear user value and maintainer-authored direction; the PR correctly uses Related because it does not resolve the linked report’s lease stall or backport. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 4 items remain** Keep this PR open: it addresses a confirmed rollback defect, but introduces a shipped-updater compatibility regression and breaks the extracted PR wrapper’s import closure. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `59c8fb01c2e8ad2b7f27ef0a7b9d61567077150c` ## Before merge - [ ] **Preserve the shipped post-core handoff without a transported executor (P1)** - The published 2026.9.3 updater spawns the candidate’s `update` CLI with `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_POST_CORE=1`, a run ID, and result-file paths, but no executor object. `resumePostCoreUpdate` only acquires an executor for the 2026.9.2 legacy bridge, so the 2026.9.3 route reaches this new guard without `opts.run.executorFence` and fails before plugin convergence. Existing older-parent caller tests fail at this line in exact-head CI. Preserve that shipped route through the existing authority owner; an older installed updater cannot be changed by its candidate. - [ ] **Include the new config dependency in the extracted wrapper sources (P1)** - This eager import adds `plugin-cohort-publication.ts` and its recovery dependencies to a module included in the trusted PR wrapper, but the PR leaves `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` unchanged. The extracted wrapper therefore cannot resolve this import. Exact-head CI confirms both the unresolved module and missing transitive closure in the wrapper inventory tests. Update the inventory or narrow the dependency boundary so extracted consumers retain a complete runtime graph. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade. Show that existing data still loads and works with this change. - [ ] **Explain or restore the original intent of Shipped post-core completion** - unknown: The published 2026.9.3 caller and existing compatibility tests establish a child-owned post-core handoff without a transported executor; local history could not establish its introduction because older blobs were unavailable. ## Findings - [P1] Preserve the shipped post-core handoff without a transported executor — `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-resume.ts:521-526` - [P1] Include the new config dependency in the extracted wrapper sources — `src/config/mutate.include-io.ts:32` ### Provenance - `Shipped post-core completion` changes intended behavior without addressing why it exists (unknown: The published 2026.9.3 caller and existing compatibility tests establish a child-owned post-core handoff without a transported executor; local history could not establish its introduction because older blobs were unavailable.) ### Tests - Low-value test `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-convergence-authority.test.ts`: Remove the added adopted-finalization table at lines 137–153: it checks a requiresCohort argument sent to a mocked producer, while the persistence suite exercises actual acceptance and refusal. - Missing end-to-end proof: Public source-bound output is still needed for the reported latest-stable upgrade and persisted recovery preservation; the shipped 2026.9.3 handoff also needs regression validation after repair.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The updater coordinates package activation, Doctor, plugin installation, database backups, and Gateway readiness; recovery restores owned changes under the existing executor and plugin lifecycle lease. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Core updater] --> B[Verified database backup] B --> C[Plugin recovery journal] C --> D[Doctor and plugin installation] D --> E[Gateway activation verification] E --> F[Commit retained cohort] E --> G[Restore previous cohort] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep recovery in the existing update, plugin, and config owners while preserving shipped-parent handoffs and completing the wrapper’s source inventory. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? The linked report establishes incompatible plugins surviving core rollback, and current-main rollback restores package/config/database state without a retained plugin-cohort restoration path. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Durable preimages and fresh lease acquisition address interrupted recovery appropriately, but the new guard must accommodate the verified shipped-parent contract and the config imports must remain available to extracted consumers. Full review comments: - [P1] Preserve the shipped post-core handoff without a transported executor — `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-resume.ts:521-526` The published 2026.9.3 updater spawns the candidate’s `update` CLI with `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_POST_CORE=1`, a run ID, and result-file paths, but no executor object. `resumePostCoreUpdate` only acquires an executor for the 2026.9.2 legacy bridge, so the 2026.9.3 route reaches this new guard without `opts.run.executorFence` and fails before plugin convergence. Existing older-parent caller tests fail at this line in exact-head CI. Preserve that shipped route through the existing authority owner; an older installed updater cannot be changed by its candidate. Confidence: 0.98 - [P1] Include the new config dependency in the extracted wrapper sources — `src/config/mutate.include-io.ts:32` This eager import adds `plugin-cohort-publication.ts` and its recovery dependencies to a module included in the trusted PR wrapper, but the PR leaves `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` unchanged. The extracted wrapper therefore cannot resolve this import. Exact-head CI confirms both the unresolved module and missing transitive closure in the wrapper inventory tests. Update the inventory or narrow the dependency boundary so extracted consumers retain a complete runtime graph. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.96 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. The daily update matrix found that this change breaks native `openclaw update` from every current stable release, so I'm reverting it in #189617.

**Symptom.** The released updaters for 2026.10.7, 10.8 and 10.9 drive the first hop of the update. Updating with them to a main build that contains this commit fails, 3 out of 3 times on Linux, and Windows 10.9 fails the same way:

- The update fails in about 280 s with `state-migrated-no-rollback`.
- The candidate Doctor refuses with `SQLite migration source changed after update capture: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`.
- The Gateway is left stopped.

Updates from 9.9 and 9.36 still pass.

**Bisect.** I ran the native 10.9 lane on Linux Crabbox, with packages built from source.

- Passes: `a5d66ef`, the parent of this commit, and every earlier commit I tested.
- Fails: `6fd646e`, which is this commit, and every later main commit I tested.

Instrumentation showed the state database already differed from the installed updater's capture when the candidate Doctor started, before any migration ran. The only logical difference was the `update_runs` row.

**Proof of the revert.** I restored the same 10.9 snapshot and ran `openclaw update --tag` with the installed 10.9 updater.

- To main `0fa8b191def`: rc=1, the Gateway is stopped.
- To the revert branch: rc=0, verification recorded, the Gateway is active and `readyz` reports ready.

**What a redesign needs.** The plugin-restore goal still needs to land. The released updater captures the state database before the candidate code runs, so a redesign must not write to that database before Doctor admits the candidate. The "older-released-parent gap" noted in this PR's description is the path every user takes on their first update.

An update on my earlier comment: no revert is needed. The cause was the native state-database read at the start of the delegated Doctor (`withPluginCohortConfigCapture` with `allowNativeRead: true`), which changed the installed updater's captured file generation before Doctor's migration capture. #190179 (`9172615f1db`) fixes it by using the snapshot read, so the plugin-restore behavior stays. I've closed revert PR #189617.

One related item remains, outside #188978's scope. `update-candidate-predecessor-stop` records a run step through `recordUpdateRunStepAsync` before Doctor's capture whenever it stops a live supervised predecessor. That write predates this change. It doesn't fire on the native lane I tested, because the updater stops the Gateway first. It is tracked for the update sweep's next run.
